sources.facts: Archaeological Survey of India identifies the irregular octagon, two principal gates, red sandstone walls, marble waterfront pavilions and Diwan-i-Am with nine arches and three aisles.
World Heritage record distinguishes Shah Jahan’s palace fort and Salimgarh as linked heritage sites. The surviving pavilion complex incorporates Persian, Timurid and Indian architecture.
Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage records the 10.5 m Lahori barbican, main three-storey gate with octagonal flanks and domed chhatris, and the separate Delhi Gate.
Historic published survey records the north-facing barbican entrance, west-facing Lahori gate and a 52 ft by 27 ft bridge. Consulted written survey facts only.
Government heritage statement identifies the long sandstone walls on the east and west and octagonal plan.
